title: 3 Cores, 600 Grains… Who Becomes the Biggest? 🤯
description:
Which core becomes a star: blue, red or gold? Comment your pick before the dust starts to merge!

Three colored cores sit in a rotating disc of 600 dust grains. This is a toy model, not real astrophysics: real stars do not form by pairwise merging, and the mass numbers are arbitrary. Every body pulls on every other body with softened inverse-square gravity. When two bodies touch they merge and keep their total mass and momentum. Dust has no color, so a merge with dust keeps the core's color; when two cores merge the heavier one keeps its color and the other is swallowed. Bodies change form at mass tiers: rock, then moon at 6, planet at 30 and giant at 100, and each step up pops a name tag. The three bars at the bottom show every core's mass from the first frame, and the first core to reach mass 250 ignites: it flashes into a star and a shockwave blows the rest away. Then the dust drifts back into the opening disc.
Gravity, picture and sound are generated by code (seed 155), with no footage, samples or stock media.
Which core did you pick?
#simulation #satisfying #space
